points.description: States that a pointer is initialized/set to point to the first element of the array (i.e., the array's base address, e.g. p = arr or p = &arr[0]).
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if a pointer to the array is mentioned but the first element/base address is not stated precisely.

points.description: States that the pointer is then incremented/offset by the index of the array element (e.g. *(p + i) or *(arr + i)) to reach that element.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if offsetting/adding to the pointer is mentioned but the index as the offset is not stated precisely.

points.description: Makes clear that the offset (index) is added to the pointer and the result is dereferenced to access the element, distinct from subscript notation arr[i].

rubric.notes: Full marks need the precise two-part fact: a pointer set to the first element (base address), then offset by the index (e.g. *(p+i)). Vague statements such as "use pointers" earn nothing; give part marks only where clearly more than half of a point is stated precisely. A wrong statement on a point (e.g. pointer set to the last element) earns nothing for that point.
